history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE — this row duplicates seq 1038 (Unakoti, near Kailashahar); see data/json/1038.json (on the Mac output folder) as the canonical record. No site named Unakoti exists at Ambassa — Unakoti is the famous rock-cut Shaivite sculpture site ~8 km from Kailashahar in Unakoti district, ~178 km from Agartala and far from Ambassa (Dhalai district); the CSV town 'Ambassa' is wrong and has been corrected. Bas-relief rock carvings ascribed on stylistic grounds to 7th-9th century CE (pre-Manikya period; one account credits patronage by the Deva dynasty of Sribhumi in Samatata — verify). 'Unakoti' means 'one less than a crore': legend says Shiva, travelling to Kashi with a crore gods and goddesses, rested here overnight and cursed the sleepers into stone at sunrise. Features giant Shiva faces, Ganesha, Durga, Vishnu and Nandi carvings plus waterfalls and kundas; ASI-protected and on the UNESCO World Heritage tentative list since 2022; the Asokastami festival is held here.
